title: Roadmap Resilience Simulation & KPI Cheatsheet
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, operational cheatsheet for running constraint-driven roadmap simulations and quick KPI checks ahead of feature launches. Focus is on tradeoffs (latency vs cost vs quality) and prescriptive mitigations when an indicator crosses a threshold. Use this as the go/no-go input for canary decisions and as a simulation spec for SRE/infra experiments.

Audience: product-ops, SRE, serving-runtime, release engineers, launch lead.

Scope:
- Short, repeatable sim scenarios that map to realistic constraints (GPU pool saturations, long-sequence prompts, KV-cache misses, regional outages).
- Key KPIs and triggers for mitigation and rollout gating.
- Lightweight checklist for pre-launch and fast triage during rollout.

Quick summary (one-liner):
Run targeted constraint sims, evaluate the KPI matrix below, run mitigations in order (cache tuning -> batching -> fallback model -> rate-limit), and use the readiness checklist for go/no-go.

Assumptions:
- Baseline traffic profile is the last 7 days 95th-percentile from production.
- Model variants: base-v1 (high quality), base-v1-quant (lower cost), base-v1-fallback (smaller, lower latency).
- Infrastructure: Dedicated GPU pool with burst capacity; autoscaler configured but intentionally capped for sim to test failure modes.

Key scenarios to simulate (short names):
1) single-region-congestion: 20% of traffic pinned to one AZ, GPU saturates -> measure latency and error propagation
2) long-sequence-surge: 8x increase in average tokens/req (e.g., long context) -> measure token-cost and p95 latency
3) cache-cold-start: deliberate eviction of prefix cache -> measure throughput drop and CPU/GPU spikes
4) quant-regression-check: switch to quantized model under load -> measure quality delta and hallucination rate
5) network-degradation: introduce 200ms cross-region RTT -> observe tail latency and retry amplification

KPI matrix (use as evaluation table after each sim):
KPI | target | critical trigger (mitigate) | owner
-------------------------------------------------------------
p95 latency (ms) | <= 350ms | > 600ms sustained for 3m | eng-serving-runtime
99th latency (ms) | <= 1.2s | > 2.0s for 5m | eng-sre
Token cost per 1k (USD) | <= $0.30 | > $0.50 and rising | product-ops
Error rate (5xx + timeouts) | < 0.5% | > 2% | eng-platform
Throughput (req/s) | within 15% of expected | drop > 40% | release-eng
Cache hit rate (prefix + KV) | > 85% | < 60% | eng-serving-runtime
Model quality delta (A/B eval) | < 1.5 pts loss | > 3 pts lost | applied-ml
Customer-visible failures | 0 | any customer-impacting failure | customer-success

Simulation runbook (compact):
- Input: traffic shape file (see linked artifacts), model variant, infra cap config.
- Steps:
  1) Snapshot baseline KPIs (10m sample) and take a quick artifact ID (logs/trace link).
  2) Apply scenario traffic generator (locust/tsunami) with config for 20m run (short sim).
  3) Monitor KPIs in realtime dashboard and annotate events in the sim log.
  4) If a critical trigger fires, pause sim and run mitigations listed below in priority order; re-run for 10m after each mitigation.
  5) Capture final KPI matrix and tag outcome: PASS / PARTIAL / FAIL.

Priority mitigations (order matters):
- M1: KV/prefix cache warmup and increase RPC timeouts by 15% (fastest, low risk).
- M2: Adjust batching window (reduce latency-sensitive batching, or increase to improve throughput) per workload profile.
- M3: Route a portion (20-40%) of traffic to quantized model variant for cost relief while monitoring quality delta.
- M4: Enable regional spillover (route to secondary region) for availability, watch for increased RTT.
- M5: Apply conservative rate-limits and graceful degradation (shorter responses, structured partial outputs).

Launch readiness quick checklist (use before canary and at 25/50/100% ramp):
- Telemetry: dashboards have the scenario KPIs and thresholds wired (Y/N) -> Owner: eng-observability
- Canary plan: traffic slices and rollback plan in linear/jira (Y/N) -> Owner: release-eng
- Mitigation playbook attached to incident runbook (Y/N) -> Owner: eng-sre
- Model validation: automated eval sets cover critical prompts (Y/N) -> Owner: applied-ml
- Cost guardrails: token-budget alerts configured (Y/N) -> Owner: finance-eng
- Customer comms template ready if degraded (Y/N) -> Owner: customer-success
- Security/PII: no new data flows introduced by this rollout (Y/N) -> Owner: security

Go/no-go heuristics (quick):
- If p95 latency > 600ms OR error rate > 2% during a 10m canary -> HOLD and investigate.
- If model-quality delta > 3 pts on core eval set -> ROLLBACK candidate.
- If token cost per 1k above threshold and no mitigations available -> SLOW RAMP and engage product for tradeoff decision.

Triage decision ladder (example for single-region-congestion):
1) Confirm metric (false positives from dashboards) -> check raw logs and traces.
2) Try M1 (cache warmup). If p95 improves to <500ms -> Continue partial ramp.
3) If still high, apply M2 (batch tuning) for 10m test.
4) If still high and throughput is bottlenecked, trigger M4 (regional spillover) + notify support.

Simple simulation config snippets (notes for infra team):
- traffic-shape: {peak:1.6, sustained:1.2, long_seq_ratio:0.12} -> map to loadgen file name: sim-longseq-A.json (see Confluence)
- infra-cap: {gpu_pool_cap: 18, max_autoscale: 22} -> used to test saturation without unlimited autoscale
- model-switch-window: 60s (how quickly to ramp traffic to fallback)

Post-sim deliverable checklist (what product-ops needs to publish):
- Short result memo (1 page) with PASS/PARTIAL/FAIL + recommended rollout cadence.
- KPI CSV exported and attached to sim ticket.
- Incidents or mitigations used logged in Jira with cost delta estimate.
- Follow-up action items assigned with owners and ETA.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a small canonical eval set for quantized-regression check (assigned to Ruth).
- Validate cost model for token pricing across model variants (finance + product ops).
- Add an automated smoke test that runs M1 after every deploy (SRE task).
- Confirm owner for customer comms template localization (CS owner).

Notes to self / quick links: 
- Slack thread: #prod-ops/t/roadmap-resilience (bookmark)
- Confluence sim playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PROD/Resilience-Sims
- Example sim ticket: JIRA-OPS-987

Sign-off: Maya T. (product-ops)

-- end of cheatsheet --
